"Prototype Phase 008: WASM Backend Planning reaches the real FedosWasmLoader — planLoad() actually called, BlockedByPolicy, a pre-existing call-graph cycle discovered and fixed" ([`src/runtime/fedos_wasm_backend.ts`](src/runtime/fedos_wasm_backend.ts), [`src/runtime/fedos_wasm_loader.ts`](src/runtime/fedos_wasm_loader.ts), [`src/runtime/fedos_explicit_crypto_initialization.ts`](src/runtime/fedos_explicit_crypto_initialization.ts), [`src/runtime/runtime_crypto_diagnostics.ts`](src/runtime/runtime_crypto_diagnostics.ts), [`docs/runtime_wasm_backend_planning.md`](docs/runtime_wasm_backend_planning.md), [`docs/runtime_internal_execution_contract.md`](docs/runtime_internal_execution_contract.md), [`test/`](test/)). The FIRST real connection from the Prototype Phase arc to a previously-"unwired" file: `Runtime → initializeCrypto() → Crypto Loader Facade → Crypto Loader Backend Abstraction → Backend Interface → WASM Backend Planning → FedosWasmLoader.planLoad() → BlockedByPolicy → STOP`. `src/runtime/fedos_wasm_backend.ts`'s `createWasmBackend()` (Stage 793) now constructs a `FedosWasmLoader` (`fedos_wasm_loader.ts`, Stage 489–492) and calls its `planLoad()` — DISCARDING the `{ operation: "load", state: "BlockedByPolicy", policy: "FailClosed", reason: "..." }` result and keeping its OWN return value byte-for-byte unchanged (`{ state: "PlanningOnly", backendReady: false, loaderAttached: false, loaderKind: "WasmLoaderPlanned", reason: "WasmBackendPlanningPending" }`). **Implementing this exposed a genuine pre-existing bug**: `planLoad()`'s own internal chain (the WASM Loader Activation arc, 13 files) terminates at `fedos_dynamic_loader_dev_approval.ts` calling `fedos_explicit_crypto_initialization.ts`, which — since Stage 595 — ALSO called `createCryptoLoaderFacade()`. That reach was harmless as long as nothing upstream of the Facade ever called back down into that arc; connecting `fedos_wasm_backend.ts` (reachable FROM the Facade) to `planLoad()` closed the loop into a cycle (Facade → Backend → Interface → WASM Backend → WASM Loader → … → Explicit Crypto Initialization → Facade → …), causing unbounded recursion and a stack overflow on every call to `createCryptoLoaderFacade()`/`AppRuntime.initializeCrypto()`. Caught before any commit via the new test suite; user confirmed the fix — **Stage 793 REMOVES the Stage 595 reach**: `fedos_explicit_crypto_initialization.ts` no longer imports or calls `fedos_crypto_loader_facade.ts`, and is now a TERMINUS calling nothing further, exactly as `docs/runtime_internal_execution_contract.md`'s own Stage 585–589 target diagram always depicted it (that diagram never showed the Stage 595 reach to begin with). `createExplicitCryptoInitialization()`'s own return value is unchanged. `src/runtime/runtime_crypto_diagnostics.ts` (Stage 793) adds `wasmBackendLoaderReached`/`wasmBackendLoaderLoaded`/`wasmBackendLoaderDecision` (fixed `true`/`false`/`"BlockedByPolicy"`) to `RuntimeCryptoActivationStatus`/`runtimeCryptoActivationStatus()` — `worker_crypto_diagnostics.ts` is intentionally NOT touched. `docs/runtime_wasm_backend_planning.md` gains a new §6 ("Loader reached, still blocked") and `docs/runtime_internal_execution_contract.md` gains a new "Prototype Phase 008" update section documenting both the real Loader connection AND the discovered-and-fixed cycle, plus a historical correction to its own Stage 593–597 section. New `test/runtime_wasm_backend_loader_connection.test.ts` (16 tests) and existing-suite updates guard: `FedosWasmLoaderSkeleton.planLoad()` is actually invoked (verified via spy) and its result discarded; `createWasmBackend()`'s own fixed value is unchanged, including across repeated calls; the new standalone accessors report reached/not-loaded/BlockedByPolicy; the real Loader's own behavior is completely unchanged; the FULL reach chain (Runtime→Facade→Backend→Interface→WasmBackend→WasmLoader) terminates normally with NO stack overflow, and `fedos_explicit_crypto_initialization.ts`'s source no longer references the Facade; diagnostics match and Worker diagnostics carry NONE of the three new fields; the WASM Backend source legitimately reaches only `fedos_wasm_loader.ts` itself (never `fedos_wasm_loader_plan.ts`/`fedos_wasm_loader_contract.ts` directly, never the generated JS glue, `WebAssembly`, or Rust); `WebAssembly.instantiate`/`compile` and `fetch` are never invoked exercising the full chain through the real Loader; Runtime/Worker remain fully unconnected to it; `encrypt`/`decrypt` unchanged; `"Allowed"`/`"Loaded"`/`"Active"` unreachable anywhere in the chain; Rust public API unchanged (27 `pub fn`) and Cargo/package dependencies unchanged; both docs record the required facts. One pre-existing test (`test/runtime_wasm_backend.test.ts` #3) is updated in place to reflect that `fedos_wasm_backend.ts` now legitimately references `fedos_wasm_loader.ts` (previously forbidden, now Stage 793's own real wiring) while still never touching its downstream files directly — the ONLY change in that file. Two exact-diagnostics-snapshot tests gain the three new fields. Verification: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` green (217 files / 3315 tests); `cargo check` (native) green; `packages/fedos-core-rust/target`/`Cargo.lock`/`pkg` (all gitignored) deleted and confirmed absent as the final step; `git status --short` clean after commit. **Still true**: no Runtime/Worker connection change of any kind (`create_runtime.ts`/`src/worker.ts` reference neither `fedos_wasm_backend.ts` nor `fedos_wasm_loader.ts`); the generated JS glue, `WebAssembly.instantiate`/`compile`, `initSync`/the default init export, and Rust remain completely unreached (`planLoad()` stops at its own internal Loader Plan); no static or dynamic `import()` of the generated JS glue; no generated file edited or committed; `encrypt`/`decrypt` unchanged; NIP-17/NIP-44/NIP-59, Double Ratchet, Triple Ratchet, and onion routing unimplemented; Rust public API unchanged (27 `pub fn`); no `Cargo.toml`/`package.json` dependency added. ✓

1012. Compares all eleven required criteria (Forward Compatibility, Versioning, Storage, Network, Worker, Production, Fail Closed, Serializer責務, Deserializer責務, Rust Boundary, JS Boundary, Runtime Boundary) across all six candidates in one table, concluding CBOR would very likely require a genuinely new `[dependencies]` crate (triggering `docs/rust_dependency_adoption.md`'s own adoption-review bar, forbidden this Stage) and a Fixed Binary Envelope would re-derive, from zero, a Fail-Closed decoder discipline Stage 186 already built, tested, and fixed once — while reusing the existing JSON codec inherits an ALREADY-PROVEN Deserializer for free. Answers five specifically-posed questions: (1) building `exportCiphertext()` alone first is REJECTED — export-without-import is not independently useful the way `encrypt()`-without-`decrypt()` was (Alpha 009 §6/Alpha 011 §6's staged-Alpha precedent does not transfer to a serialization PAIR, where one half produces useless byte soup nobody can ever reverse); (2) export/import MUST always ship together as a standing rule for any future serialization boundary this arc adds; (3) a version byte IS necessary from the very first shipped format — retrofitting one later is the SAME "breakage deferred is breakage compounded" pattern Alpha 012 §2 already established for the key-boundary migration, and `AeadEnvelopeVersion`/Stage 182's version-first-checked discipline already exist to reuse; (4) version/algorithm-label/aadDomain-label/nonce/ciphertext/tag ALL belong on the wire (restating Stage 182 §3/§4's exact field list and exclusions — no `kid`, no secret byte, no plaintext/content-type hint, no payment/chat metadata); (5) exposing Rust's internal Envelope type directly IS forbidden, reaffirming Alpha 014's own opaque-wrapper forbid-list and `docs/public_crypto_opaque_handles.md` §2 — any future `exportCiphertext()` must go through the SAME reviewed codec, never a `Debug`-derived dump or raw struct-to-object shortcut. Lays out the Fail-Closed Serializer/Deserializer split: the Serializer's obligation is narrow (never panic, never emit what its own paired Deserializer cannot read back — its input is always already-trusted internal state); the Deserializer carries the PRIMARY Fail-Closed burden (its input is untrusted by construction) and should split a SAFE, distinguishable structural rejection (bad wire shape — reveals nothing about key material) from the SAME undistinguishable cryptographic no-oracle outcome `decrypt()` already uses (Alpha 015), mirroring `InvalidKeyHandle`/`InvalidCiphertextHandle` vs. the collapsed `DecryptionFailed` precedent exactly. **Recommends Alpha 017 be a dedicated Ciphertext Wire Format DECISION (mirroring Alpha 012's own role after Alpha 011) that formally ADOPTS reusing the Stage 182/186 codec for a NEW `exportCiphertext()`/`importCiphertext()` pair — not implementation directly** — because this arc's own established discipline (review → decision → implementation, per Alpha 007/009/011 → 012 → 013) never skips the decision stage, and several concrete choices (exact `#[wasm_bindgen]` wrapper names/signatures, `Uint8Array`-of-UTF8-bytes vs. plain `string` JS return type, new Loader execution-result interfaces' own Fail-Closed reason enumerations) still need to be FORMALLY FIXED, not merely leaned toward, before any code is authorized. 1013. "Secure Runtime Alpha 017: Public Runtime Ciphertext Wire Format Decision — REVIEW/DESIGN DECISION ONLY, formally adopting Alpha 016's own recommendation across ten decided items, executing (not merely leaning toward) the review's conclusions before any code exists" ([`docs/secure_runtime_alpha_017_ciphertext_wire_format_decision.md`](docs/secure_runtime_alpha_017_ciphertext_wire_format_decision.md), [`test/secure_runtime_alpha_017_ciphertext_wire_format_decision.test.ts`](test/secure_runtime_alpha_017_ciphertext_wire_format_decision.test.ts)). Decides: (1) **Wire Format** — the existing canonical JSON+base64url format (Stage 182/186, `v`/`alg`/`aad`/`n`/`ct`/`tag`) is formally adopted as Secure Runtime's own Public Ciphertext Wire Format; no new format is created or authorized. (2) **Public Runtime API** — `exportCiphertext(ciphertext: AeadCiphertextHandle): Promise<AeadCiphertextWire | null>` / `importCiphertext(serialized: AeadCiphertextWire): Promise<AeadCiphertextHandle | null>`, symmetric with `encrypt()`/`decrypt()`'s own shape. (3) **JS Wire type** — a plain `string` is adopted; `Uint8Array` is rejected (would force an unreviewed, benefit-free UTF-8 round trip through bytes, undoing Stage 182's own text-safety rationale); a dedicated parsed object is rejected (would re-implement a JSON parser in TypeScript, bypassing Rust's already-reviewed Deserializer, functionally equivalent to the raw-envelope-exposure Alpha 016 §3.5 already forbade). (4) **Branding** — `type AeadCiphertextWire = string & { readonly __brand: "AeadCiphertextWire" }` is ADOPTED, explicitly documented as a COMPILE-TIME API-misuse boundary only, NEVER a runtime security boundary — all real Fail-Closed enforcement stays entirely inside Rust's `decode_envelope_internal`, unaffected by whether a caller obtained the brand honestly or via a bypass cast. (5) **Rust `wasm-bindgen` wrapper contract** (decided, not implemented) — `serialize_aead_ciphertext(ciphertext: &AeadCiphertextHandle) -> Option<String>` calling `encode_envelope_internal(ciphertext.inner().inner())` exactly once, and `deserialize_aead_ciphertext(serialized: &str) -> Option<AeadCiphertextHandle>` calling `decode_envelope_internal(serialized)` exactly once, constructing a NEW `AeadCiphertextHandle` via the SAME plain struct-literal pattern `encrypt_aead()` already uses on `CiphertextSerializationStatus::Valid` — confirmed by inspection to need no new Rust logic beyond the wrapper itself, and confirmed consistent with `FedosCiphertextEnvelope::from_inner`'s own pre-existing doc comment reserving exactly this future stage. (6) **Fail-Closed reason model** — `FedosWasmLoaderExportCiphertextExecution`/`ImportCiphertextExecution` decided, mirroring `EncryptExecution`/`DecryptExecution`'s own established shape exactly (uniform `"Succeeded"` tag, split `PrototypeStillClosed`/`NotInitialized` early gate, pre-call vs. post-call shape checks named `InvalidWireInputShape`/`InvalidHandleOutputShape` for the import direction specifically) — refining the originally-proposed `"Exported"`/`"Imported"`/`"NotReady"`/`"InvalidHandleShape"` labels to match precedent, with reasoning recorded for each refinement; the Public API itself surfaces NONE of these reasons, only `... | null`. (7) **Export/Import implementation unit** — DECIDED: designed AND implemented together in the SAME Stage (Alpha 018), executing Alpha 016 §3.1/§3.2 directly; explicitly separates this from commit-level granularity, which MAY still be split across several commits within that one Stage, so long as no intermediate state ships one direction as a usable Public API while the other is absent. (8) **Trust Boundary** — spelled out per direction: export accepts ONLY a structurally-genuine `AeadCiphertextHandle`, never touches a raw byte outside the reviewed codec, and its Serializer never panics, returning only round-trip-capable output; import treats its input as COMPLETELY untrusted, rejecting unknown version/algorithm/AAD-domain labels, malformed base64url, and wrong nonce/tag/ciphertext lengths, deferring unknown/missing-field handling entirely to the existing codec's own strict behavior, with no exception ever escaping. (9) **Crypto-failure separation** — DECIDED explicitly: `importCiphertext()` validates wire STRUCTURE only and performs no AEAD operation; a wire value CAN and WILL import successfully even if it will later fail `decrypt()`'s own authentication check (wrong key, wrong AAD, tampering) — stated as BY DESIGN, not a gap, since import succeeding is a necessary but never sufficient precondition for a later `decrypt()` success, preserving Alpha 015's own no-oracle discipline undiluted. (10) **Storage/Network/Worker/future consumers** — surveyed (Secure Storage, Network transport, Worker `postMessage`, Runtime-restart recovery, Marketplace content delivery, DM, BBS-style content posting) as consumers this text-safe, structured-clone-safe `string` shape correctly prepares for, with NONE connected by this Stage. Cross-checks consistency against Stage 182/186, Alpha 013/014/015/016, `docs/ciphertext_envelope_plan.md`, and `docs/public_crypto_opaque_handles.md` explicitly, item by item. **Recommends Alpha 018 implement the Rust wrapper pair AND the full Public Runtime API together, in one Stage** — rejecting 'Rust wrappers only, Public API later' (reproduces the exact 'codec wired to nothing' problem one layer up), rejecting 'export side only' (fails Stage 182's own round-trip-provable-before-shipping bar outright), and rejecting a further review/decision Stage (every consequential choice is now formally fixed; nothing remains that would justify repeating Alpha 011→012's discipline for no new open question). New `test/secure_runtime_alpha_017_ciphertext_wire_format_decision.test.ts` (26 tests) guards: the decision doc exists and is substantial; states REVIEW/DESIGN DECISION ONLY with an explicit does-not-implement list; confirms all ten decided items by their exact conclusions, code contracts, and rejected alternatives; confirms the real Rust functions (`encode_envelope_internal`/`decode_envelope_internal`/`FedosCiphertextEnvelope::from_inner`/`encrypt_aead`'s own struct-literal pattern) this decision's wrapper contract depends on exist exactly as described, unchanged; confirms zero `exportCiphertext`/`importCiphertext`/`serialize_aead_ciphertext`/`deserialize_aead_ciphertext` identifier exists anywhere in the real Runtime/Loader/Worker/Rust surface; reconfirms all six existing Crypto API fields/behaviors unchanged by ACTUAL calls; still exactly seven `FedosWasmLoader` Plan interfaces; Rust/Cargo/package sources confirmed unchanged at 34 `pub fn`, eleven `#[wasm_bindgen]`, 11/2 dependencies; confirms no new dependency is proposed anywhere in this decision. Verification: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` green, zero regressions; `cargo check` (native) green; `packages/fedos-core-rust/target`/`Cargo.lock`/`pkg` (all gitignored) deleted after verification; `git status --short` clean after commit. **Still true**: every Public API and Fail-Closed guarantee from Alpha 001–016 byte-for-byte unchanged; no Worker/Production/Secure Storage/Network connection of any kind; `exportCiphertext()`/`importCiphertext()`/`importKey()`/`exportKey()` all remain unimplemented; `Cargo.toml`/`package.json` unchanged (no new dependency). **This Stage closes the decision gap Alpha 016 opened — every concrete choice an Alpha 018 implementer needs (wire format, API signature, JS type, branding, Rust contract, Fail-Closed model, shipping unit, trust boundary, and the crypto/wire failure split) is now fixed in writing, so Alpha 018 can implement directly against this document rather than making any of these calls inline.** ✓

Unlike every prior Crypto API in this arc, this Stage reaches NO `FedosWasmLoader` and NO Rust Boundary at all: `exportCiphertext()`/`importCiphertext()` (Stage 1011) already complete the one and only WASM/Rust round trip a ciphertext wire value ever needs, so storing/loading/deleting the resulting plain `string` requires no cryptographic operation — `packages/fedos-core-rust/src/lib.rs`/`Cargo.toml`/`package.json` are all byte-for-byte UNCHANGED by this Stage, confirmed by inspection (no ripple of any kind followed, unlike every prior Rust-touching Stage). New `src/runtime/fedos_runtime_ciphertext_storage.ts` (the 50th `fedos_*.ts` file) defines, in one file (mirroring `fedos_wasm_loader.ts`'s own "interface + implementation together" convention): a `RuntimeCiphertextStorage` Storage Interface (`store`/`load`/`delete`, each keyed by a caller-supplied `id: string`); `MemoryCiphertextStorage`, the ONLY backend this Stage ships — a plain in-process `Map`, explicitly NOT SQLite/IndexedDB/filesystem/Windows DPAPI/macOS Keychain/Linux Secret Service, none of which is implemented; and the three exported functions themselves, each performing its OWN, directly analogous `process.env.NODE_ENV` read (mirroring `FedosWasmLoaderSkeleton#evaluateDevOnlyGate()`/`determineRuntimeMode()`'s own Fail-Closed try/catch shape exactly, since there is no Loader to reach for this gate) as the Development-Runtime gate, plus an `id`/`wire` non-empty-`string` shape guard, plus a `try`/`catch` around every storage-backend call — Fail Closed to `null` (never `false`) on any of: not Development Runtime; invalid `id`/`wire` shape; the storage backend itself throwing. **STORES `AeadCiphertextWire` ONLY — `AeadKeyHandle` storage remains permanently forbidden**, enforced at the type level (`store(id: string, wire: AeadCiphertextWire)` — passing an `AeadKeyHandle` is a compile-time error, not merely a documented rule); `exportKey()`/`importKey()` remain unimplemented and are not made any more reachable. **Deliberate, explicitly documented exception to this arc's own "fresh instance per call" convention**: every prior Crypto API's Runtime Service constructs a BRAND NEW `FedosWasmLoader` on every call; Storage's entire purpose is the opposite (`storeCiphertext()` now, `loadCiphertext()` later must observe the SAME data), so this file's default storage (`defaultCiphertextStorage`) is a SINGLE, shared, module-level `MemoryCiphertextStorage` instance — confined entirely to this one file, and confirmed by a dedicated test that two separate calls omitting the `storage` parameter observe each other's writes. `src/runtime/types.ts` adds all three fields to `AppRuntime`, importing NO new type (reusing the already-imported `AeadCiphertextWire`), with each field's own doc comment restating the `AeadCiphertextWire`-only restriction. `src/runtime/create_runtime.ts` imports and wires all three, its own new doc-comment block avoiding the literal `AeadCiphertextWire` substring (its lowercase form collides with a pre-existing `aeadcipher` guard check, the SAME lexical trap Alpha 015 already found and fixed once) by paraphrasing as "the exported ciphertext wire value `exportCiphertext`/`importCiphertext` already produce/consume." New `docs/secure_runtime_alpha_019_secure_storage_foundation.md` documents the shorter (Rust-Boundary-free) architecture, the Storage Interface and sole backend, the `AeadCiphertextWire`-only restriction, the singleton exception, the full Fail-Closed table, and the round-trip completion criterion. New `test/secure_runtime_alpha_019_secure_storage_foundation.test.ts` (24 tests) guards: the design doc exists, is substantial, and states every required disclosure; against the real repo state, invalid-shape calls resolve `null` in Development; a REAL mocked round trip (`encrypt()` → `exportCiphertext()` → `storeCiphertext()` → `loadCiphertext()` → `importCiphertext()` → `decrypt()`) recovers the EXACT original plaintext, with `storeCiphertext()`/`loadCiphertext()` exercised as genuinely pure JS (no WASM mock touched for those two steps); `storeCiphertext()` then `loadCiphertext()` returns the exact same wire, a never-stored `id` resolves `null`, `deleteCiphertext()` removes an entry and a subsequent load resolves `null`, deleting an already-absent `id` resolves `false` (not `null`, since the gate/shape checks and backend call all genuinely succeeded); the shared default storage is confirmed to persist across separate omitted-parameter calls; all three Fail Closed to `null` for non-string/empty `id`/`wire`, for a throwing injected storage backend, and for Production/Unknown Runtime even with a fully working backend present (with the pre-existing entry confirmed STILL there once Development resumes, proving Production/Unknown never actually reached the backend); `runtime.storeCiphertext()`/`loadCiphertext()`/`deleteCiphertext()` via the real `AppRuntime` object never throw; no `AeadKeyHandle`/`exportKey`/`importKey`/OS-Keychain/Secure-Enclave/SQLite/IndexedDB/filesystem/DPAPI/Secret-Service/Cloud/Network/Nostr/ActivityPub/Bluesky/Session reference exists anywhere in this Stage's own code; `RuntimeCiphertextStorage.store()`'s own signature confirmed to type-reject an `AeadKeyHandle`; `importKey()`/`exportKey()` confirmed NOT implemented; `initializeCrypto()`/`runtimeCapabilities()`/`randomBytes()`/`generateAeadKey()`/`encrypt()`/`decrypt()`/`exportCiphertext()`/`importCiphertext()` ALL EIGHT reconfirmed unchanged by ACTUAL calls after store/load/delete run first; this Stage's own functions confirmed to never import/construct `FedosWasmLoader`; the try/catch guarantee confirmed for all three exported functions; Worker/Production confirmed unconnected; still exactly seven `FedosWasmLoader` Plan interfaces; Rust/Cargo/package sources confirmed BYTE-FOR-BYTE UNCHANGED at 36 `pub fn`, thirteen `#[wasm_bindgen]`, 11/2 dependencies, with no reference to this Stage's own doc anywhere in `lib.rs`. Ripple: minimal and entirely confined to `fedos_*.ts` file-count assertions (4 files, 49→50, adding `fedos_runtime_ciphertext_storage.ts` as an EIGHTH named exception) plus one lexical-substring-collision fix in `create_runtime.ts`'s own new doc comment — NO `pub fn`/`#[wasm_bindgen]` count change anywhere, confirming this Stage's own "zero Rust change" claim empirically rather than merely by assertion. "Secure Runtime Alpha 020: Runtime Mode Authority Consolidation — consolidates the three independent `process.env.NODE_ENV` classifiers Alpha 006 (`docs/secure_runtime_alpha_006_mode_authority_review.md`) reviewed and named four trigger conditions for, into ONE shared Runtime Mode Authority, `src/runtime/fedos_runtime_mode_authority.ts`, triggered by Alpha 019's Ciphertext Storage Service satisfying trigger condition 4 (a real Fail-Closed Storage decision branching on `NODE_ENV`)" ([`docs/secure_runtime_alpha_020_runtime_mode_authority_consolidation.md`](docs/secure_runtime_alpha_020_runtime_mode_authority_consolidation.md), [`src/runtime/fedos_runtime_mode_authority.ts`](src/runtime/fedos_runtime_mode_authority.ts), [`src/runtime/fedos_wasm_loader.ts`](src/runtime/fedos_wasm_loader.ts), [`src/runtime/fedos_runtime_prototype_execution.ts`](src/runtime/fedos_runtime_prototype_execution.ts), [`src/runtime/fedos_runtime_ciphertext_storage.ts`](src/runtime/fedos_runtime_ciphertext_storage.ts), [`test/secure_runtime_alpha_020_runtime_mode_authority_consolidation.test.ts`](test/secure_runtime_alpha_020_runtime_mode_authority_consolidation.test.ts)). 1018. "Secure Runtime Alpha 022: Storage Backend Selection Policy Review — REVIEW ONLY, no code change of any kind. Compares five Storage Backend candidates (Memory/Windows DPAPI/macOS Keychain/Linux Secret Service/Browser Secure Storage) across ten criteria (Security/Portability/Runtime dependency/Worker support/Desktop support/Fail Closed/Backup/Exportability/User Experience/Implementation Complexity), decides WHERE a future backend-selection condition should live, confirms the Storage Resolver must never become a second Runtime Mode Authority, and recommends exactly one backend — Windows DPAPI — for Alpha 023 to implement" ([`docs/secure_runtime_alpha_022_storage_backend_selection_policy_review.md`](docs/secure_runtime_alpha_022_storage_backend_selection_policy_review.md), [`test/secure_runtime_alpha_022_storage_backend_selection_policy_review.test.ts`](test/secure_runtime_alpha_022_storage_backend_selection_policy_review.test.ts)). No code change of any kind — the Storage Backend Interface (`fedos_runtime_storage_backend.ts`), the Storage Resolver (`fedos_runtime_storage_resolver.ts`), the Runtime Storage Service (`fedos_runtime_ciphertext_storage.ts`), `types.ts`, `create_runtime.ts`, Worker, Rust, `Cargo.toml`, and `package.json` are all byte-for-byte unchanged; this is a documentation-only Stage, adding zero new `fedos_*.ts` files (still exactly 53). New `docs/secure_runtime_alpha_022_storage_backend_selection_policy_review.md` builds a ten-criteria comparison table across all five mandated candidates, finding: Memory (current) is Trivial complexity but Low security, acceptable only because it is already Development-limited; the three OS keystores (DPAPI/Keychain/Secret Service) each require a native bridge or OS-CLI shell-out (no pure-JS path, and none can be added without either a new dependency or a shell-out using only Node built-ins), with Secret Service having the widest Fail-Closed surface and worst portability of the three due to Linux keyring fragmentation; Browser Secure Storage requires browser-only globals absent from this repo's current Node-based Runtime test harness. Separately reviews a sixth candidate, "Test Backend," finding it redundant with the ALREADY-EXISTING injectable `storage` parameter `storeCiphertext()`/`loadCiphertext()`/`deleteCiphertext()` have carried since Alpha 019 — no dedicated Test Backend recommended. Compares four candidate locations for a future backend-selection switch (inside the Runtime Storage Service, inside the Storage Resolver, inside Worker, inside each backend's own self-detection) and adopts the Storage Resolver (`fedos_runtime_storage_resolver.ts`) as the sole correct location — exactly the seam Alpha 021 already built for this purpose — rejecting the Runtime Storage Service (would re-couple the Service to backend-selection details Alpha 021 deliberately extracted away) and Worker (remains fully unconnected per every prior Stage's own guardrail) outright. Confirms, and cross-checks by direct source inspection, that the Storage Backend Resolver answers a COMPLETELY ORTHOGONAL question from Alpha 020's Runtime Mode Authority (WHICH platform vs. WHAT environment) and must never reuse, extend, or import `determineFedosRuntimeMode()`/`fedos_runtime_mode_authority.ts` — a future platform-selection condition inside the Resolver must be its own, separately-named classifier, never a second `isProductionAllowed()`-shaped authorization function, extending Alpha 020 §4's own classifier-not-authorizer principle to this new axis. 1021. "Secure Runtime Alpha 025: Secure Storage API Scope Review — REVIEW ONLY, no code change of any kind. Classifies what the Secure Storage API can/cannot store today (exactly one storable type, `AeadCiphertextWire`, vs. seven distinct unstorable categories), compares five future storage-scope candidates, and formally confirms the Identity/Storage layering direction plus Nostr Event/DM/Attachment persistence being an Identity/Application Layer responsibility, never Storage Layer's" ([`docs/secure_runtime_alpha_025_secure_storage_api_scope_review.md`](docs/secure_runtime_alpha_025_secure_storage_api_scope_review.md), [`test/secure_runtime_alpha_025_secure_storage_api_scope_review.test.ts`](test/secure_runtime_alpha_025_secure_storage_api_scope_review.test.ts)). No code change of any kind — the Runtime Storage Service, Storage Backend Interface/implementations (`MemoryStorageBackend`/`WindowsDpapiStorageBackend`), the Storage Resolver, the Runtime Mode/Platform Authorities, `types.ts`, `create_runtime.ts`, Worker, Rust, `Cargo.toml`, and `package.json` are all byte-for-byte unchanged; this is a documentation-only Stage, adding zero new `fedos_*.ts` files (still exactly 56). New `docs/secure_runtime_alpha_025_secure_storage_api_scope_review.md` classifies the ONE storable shape (`AeadCiphertextWire`, still enforced at the type level since Alpha 019) against SEVEN distinct unstorable categories with individual reasoning for each — `AeadKeyHandle` (permanently excluded per Alpha 007 §6), `AeadCiphertextHandle` (the opaque, non-serializable pre-export handle `encrypt()` directly returns), `RuntimeCapabilities` (a deliberately always-recomputed PUBLIC REPORT per Alpha 006 §1), Runtime Mode and Runtime Platform (both deliberately-uncached CLASSIFIER results per Alpha 020/024, never meant to be stale-read from storage), and the raw `Uint8Array` outputs of `randomBytes()`/`decrypt()` (neither ever passed to any storage function anywhere in this arc — storing recovered plaintext would defeat the point of encrypting it). Builds a nine-criteria (Fail Closed/責務/Security/移植性/Storage抽象/Worker/Production/Nostr/将来性) comparison across five future storage-scope candidates — ① Ciphertextのみ (current), ② Ciphertext + Metadata, ③ Ciphertext + Identity, ④ Runtime全体, ⑤ Arbitrary Object Store — concluding ① remains correct and should stay the ONLY implemented scope, ② is the sole candidate worth a future, separately-reviewed Stage (and only once a genuine non-secret metadata need exists), and ③/④/⑤ are each PERMANENTLY REJECTED directions (not merely deprioritized): ③ would make Storage understand WHOSE ciphertext it holds, directly reversing the Identity/Storage layering; ④ would persist deliberately-always-re-evaluated Classifier results, contradicting their own core design; ⑤ would remove the type-level exclusion that makes every other row in the unstorable-categories table a compile-time guarantee rather than a runtime hope. ### Dual-Lock Activation Gate

**Two separate env vars must BOTH open before FedOS is even a
candidate — and even then, nothing activates.** `FEDOS_CRYPTO_PROVIDER`
("Lock #1") selects a provider NAME; `FEDOS_CRYPTO_ENABLED` ("Lock #2")
must equal the exact literal `"explicit-dev-only"` — every common
truthy spelling (`"true"`, `"1"`, `"on"`, `"enabled"`, ...) is rejected
on purpose, to make an accidental match effectively impossible. Setting
BOTH locks to their open values still does not start any cryptography:
`evaluateRuntimeCryptoActivation`/`evaluateWorkerCryptoActivation`
report `"ProviderUnavailable"` (no real `FedosRuntimeCryptoProvider`
implementation exists), and the bridge files were not touched this
stage, so they never even look at `FEDOS_CRYPTO_ENABLED`. `"Allowed"`
remains structurally unreturnable.

### Activation Policy

**Choosing a provider name is not the same as activating it.** Setting
`FEDOS_CRYPTO_PROVIDER=fedos` only records an intent — it does not, by
itself, start any cryptography. FedOS crypto activation requires ALL
FIVE of: (1) `FEDOS_CRYPTO_PROVIDER=fedos`, (2) the separate `enabled`
gate set to `true` (still permanently `false` today, with no env path to
`true` anywhere in this repository), (3) a real `FedosRuntimeCryptoProvider`
implementation (still `encrypt`/`decrypt` → `"Unsupported"` unconditionally),
(4) Runtime actually calling it (still never automatic), and (5) Worker
actually importing the Worker crypto boundary (still not imported at
all). `evaluateRuntimeCryptoActivation`/`evaluateWorkerCryptoActivation`
(`src/runtime/runtime_crypto_activation_policy.ts`/
`worker_crypto_activation_policy.ts`) report WHY activation is not
allowed — `"DisabledByConfig"`, `"ProviderNotSelected"`, or
`"ProviderUnavailable"` — and, per `docs/runtime_crypto_threat_model.md`'s
fail-closed design, can never report `"Allowed"` in this repository as it
exists today.

### Execution Backend Architecture

**FedOS is not "WASM-only" — FedOS is Backend-swappable.** FedOS Core
(the Rust crate at `packages/fedos-core-rust`) is the ONE AND ONLY
core, and it stays completely unaware of how any Runtime eventually
reaches it. The **Execution Backend** (`src/runtime/fedos_execution_backend.ts`,
Stage 402) is the swappable interface in between:

```
FedOS Core (Rust)
        |
Execution Backend
        |
      Runtime
```

WASM (`src/runtime/fedos_wasm_boundary.ts`, Stage 386) is the FIRST
implementation candidate for this interface — it is the only
candidate with any real (still entirely inert) placeholder code today
— but it is explicitly **not** the only one the architecture allows.
Native/Desktop and Mobile backends are named as future candidates in
`docs/runtime_execution_backend.md` (Stage 401/405); neither has a
file, dependency, or line of code anywhere in this repository. Picking
up either would mean writing a NEW backend implementation behind the
SAME `FedosExecutionBackend` interface — it would require zero changes
to FedOS Core, the Provider, or any layer above the Execution Backend.

`packages/fedos-core-rust` itself has never referenced "backend,"
"WASM," "native," or "mobile" in any capacity, and this stage does not
change that — its 27 `pub fn`s and `Cargo.toml` are byte-for-byte
unchanged.

### Future candidate boundaries (design notes only — not scheduled)

These are **exploratory** layers sketched in
[`docs/vault_crypto_identity.md`](docs/vault_crypto_identity.md). Each is a
future, opt-in boundary kept OUT of the current core; nothing here is
implemented, and none carries a security guarantee. When picked up, each lands as
an interface + mock/no-op first, with its own review, respecting all existing
guardrails.

- **Vault Boundary** — local encrypted master-seed storage unlocked by an auth
  factor (Apple ID/Passkey as *unlock only*, never a key-derivation source). No
  key custody in the app. *(Stage 33 lands the interface + no-op/in-memory
  skeleton in `src/vault/` — shapes only, still no crypto/keys/seed.)*
- **Crypto Core Boundary** — a separate Rust crate (`packages/fedos-core-rust`,
  provisional) for AEAD + KDF + secret zeroing; managed-runtime memory-zeroing
  limits are documented, not hand-waved. AEAD mandatory, XOR forbidden. *(Stage 34
  lands the `CryptoProvider` interface + `NoopCryptoProvider` in `src/crypto/` —
  a TypeScript seam that fixes the future Rust-core swap point; shapes only, still
  no real crypto/keys/randomness.)*
- **Deniable Storage Research Boundary** — threat-model study of hidden/shadow
  vaults (TrueCrypt/VeraCrypt as *reference*), with leak vectors (size/padding/
  metadata/timestamp/access-pattern) named and **no production safety claim**.
  *(Stage 40 writes this up as docs only in
  [`docs/deniable_storage_research.md`](docs/deniable_storage_research.md) — the
  forbidden `finger_id`-style branch anti-pattern, IPFS/Nostr leak risks,
  forbidden UI wording, and the preconditions for any future work. No code, no
  crypto, no storage; future separate package only.)*
- **IPFS Asset Adapter** — a future public-media adapter behind the existing
  `AssetCache` boundary (gateway/pinning, not an embedded node); non-deletability,
  liveness, and traffic-analysis risks documented. Public/unlisted bytes only.
- **Notification Bridge** — APNs/FCM/Telegram/LINE as contentless, opt-in
  notification pointers (no secrets in payloads; provider metadata leakage noted).
- **Payment / Lightning Boundary** — a future external, non-custodial payment
  seam (Breez SDK / Greenlight as investigation candidates); liquidity is the
  hard problem. No payment implemented or scheduled.
